content: Nitrofurantoin is an antibiotic that inhibits bacterial growth. It is ineffective against viral infections such as the common cold or influenza. This medication should be taken orally with food or milk as directed by your physician. Typically, it is administered four times daily to treat infections or once daily at bedtime to prevent infections. The medication should be swallowed whole, and the use of magnesium trisilicate-containing antacids should be avoided while taking it. Dosage and duration depend on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal efficacy, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If prescribed for infection prevention, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not skip doses or discontinue use without consulting your doctor. If treating an infection, complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms resolve after a few days. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. Taking the medication with food can help reduce nausea. Nitrofurantoin may cause urine to appear dark yellow or brown, which is harmless. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, it may cause severe (potentially fatal) lung problems, which can occur within the first month of treatment or after long-term use (typically six months or longer). It may also rarely lead to serious liver disease, blood disorders, or nerve problems. Additionally, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to Clostridium difficile bacteria, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Symptoms of a severe allergic reaction include rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face/tongue/throat), severe dizziness, and trouble breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before taking nitrofurantoin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Nitrofurantoin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It should not be used near or at the time of delivery (weeks 38–42 of pregnancy) due to the potential risk of hemolytic anemia in the newborn. This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on nursing infants less than one month old or those with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. If someone has overdosed and has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Lab and/or medical tests (e.g., complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, urine cultures) should be performed while taking this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store at room temperature away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
